summary: Provides a framework and requirements for using GMPLS to control flexi-grid DWDM networks, where ITU-T allows variable-width frequency slots for optical channels.

plainLanguage.summary: Flexi-grid optical networks assign channels variable amounts of spectrum. RFC 7698 explains how GMPLS control protocols should represent those channels and coordinate their use.

questions: how does gmpls control flexi-grid networks
how does gmpls control flexible optical networks
what is spectrum assignment in optical networks
what is a flexi-grid frequency slot
subtitle: A GMPLS framework for routing and assigning spectrum in flexi-grid DWDM networks

tldr.problem: Fixed-grid optical channels use fixed spectrum widths. Flexi-grid networks need control protocols that can select frequency slots with different widths and account for equipment capabilities along a path.
tldr.mechanism: The framework maps media channels and frequency slots to GMPLS concepts. It sets requirements for signaling, routing information, spectrum assignment, resizing, and link-property correlation.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7698 is an informational framework and requirements document. Companion documents define protocol extensions.

today: RFC 7698 is an Informational framework and requirements document and the batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC says actual GMPLS protocol extensions are defined in companion documents.

sections.title: What a Flexi-Grid Frequency Slot Is
sections.content:
Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) sends multiple optical signals through a fiber. A flexi-grid network can allocate variable-sized frequency ranges, called frequency slots, instead of relying only on fixed-width channels.

A frequency slot is described by a nominal central frequency and a slot width. The grid uses 6.25 GHz steps for central frequencies and a slot-width granularity of 12.5 GHz. RFC 7698 defines a framework for applying Generalized Multiprotocol Label Switching (GMPLS) to control these networks.
sections.plainLanguage: A flexi-grid assigns each optical connection a frequency range with a chosen width. The control system needs to track both where that range is centered and how wide it is.

sections.title: Media Channels and Optical Signals
sections.content:
The RFC distinguishes the media layer, which switches frequency slots, from the signal layer, which carries optical signals. A media channel represents a path through media elements such as fibers, filters, amplifiers, and switching matrices, together with its usable frequency slot.

A network media channel transports one Optical Tributary Signal (OTSi). Multiple network media channels may form a composite media channel carrying a group of OTSi over one fiber. The usable end-to-end slot depends on the frequency ranges supported by the filters along the path.
sections.plainLanguage: The media layer selects and connects frequency ranges. The signal layer carries the optical data within those ranges.

sections.title: Representing Channels in GMPLS
sections.content:
GMPLS represents a flexi-grid media channel as a Label Switched Path (LSP). A label identifies the locally selected frequency slot. Depending on node capabilities, the slot's central frequency or width may vary from hop to hop, provided the effective slot remains valid along the path.

Routing and Spectrum Assignment (RSA) determines both the route and its spectrum. The RFC describes combined RSA, separated route and spectrum assignment, and routing with distributed spectrum assignment. A Path Computation Element may compute a route, or nodes may assign spectrum hop by hop using signaling.
sections.plainLanguage: GMPLS represents an optical path as an LSP, and its label identifies a frequency slot. Route and spectrum decisions may be made together, separately, or at each hop.

sections.title: Control-Plane Requirements
sections.content:
Signaling must configure a nominal central frequency and a flexible slot width, and must collect the local slot assigned on each link. It must support setting up and resizing media channels. Routing must distribute enough information about available frequency ranges, slot widths, and node capabilities to compute paths.

The control plane should support logical associations and composite media channels. It may support neighbor discovery, and it should allow nodes at both ends of a link to correlate the properties they apply. These requirements are intended to cover different RSA models in one protocol framework.
sections.plainLanguage: Signaling must tell each node what spectrum to use and report what each link can support. Routing must share enough availability and capability information to choose a feasible path.

sections.title: Security and Manageability
sections.content:
The RFC says flexi-grid control has security considerations similar to fixed-grid GMPLS systems. Detailed spectrum and node-capability information can increase the load on routing protocols or control channels; damping and configurable thresholds can limit repeated advertisements caused by small resource changes.

Existing GMPLS management tools may need extensions to represent frequency slots and effective frequency slots. Link Management Protocol could be extended to exchange link capabilities. Data-plane OAM for optical systems is outside the IETF's scope, though the RFC 7260 framework could be applied with minor extensions.
sections.plainLanguage: Flexi-grid control can reuse existing GMPLS management and security approaches, with added support for spectrum details. Routing updates need controls to avoid excessive announcements when resources change.
